displayName: Letter 7.27 (to Sura, on ghosts and apparitions)

sentences.latin: Et mihi discendi et tibi docendi facultatem otium praebet.
sentences.english: Leisure provides both me with the chance to learn and you with the chance to teach.

sentences.latin: Igitur perquam velim scire, esse phantasmata et habere propriam figuram numenque aliquod putes an inania et vana ex metu nostro imaginem accipere.
sentences.english: Therefore I would very much like to know whether you think that ghosts exist and have their own form and some divine power, or whether they are empty and unreal and take their image from our fear.

sentences.latin: Ego ut esse credam in primis eo ducor, quod audio accidisse Curtio Rufo.
sentences.english: I am led to believe that they exist chiefly by what I hear happened to Curtius Rufus.

sentences.latin: Tenuis adhuc et obscurus, obtinenti Africam comes haeserat.
sentences.english: Still poor and unknown, he had attached himself as a companion to the man holding Africa as governor.

sentences.latin: Inclinato die spatiabatur in porticu; offertur ei mulieris figura humana grandior pulchriorque.
sentences.english: As the day was waning he was walking in a portico; the figure of a woman, larger and more beautiful than human, presented herself to him.

sentences.latin: Perterrito Africam se futurorum praenuntiam dixit: iturum enim Romam honoresque gesturum, atque etiam cum summo imperio in eandem provinciam reversurum, ibique moriturum.
sentences.english: To him in his terror she said she was Africa, foreteller of things to come: for he would go to Rome, and would hold offices, and would even return to the same province with the highest command, and there he would die.

sentences.latin: Facta sunt omnia.
sentences.english: All these things came to pass.

sentences.latin: Praeterea accedenti Carthaginem egredientique nave eadem figura in litore occurrisse narratur.
sentences.english: Furthermore, as he was approaching Carthage and getting off the ship, the same figure is said to have met him on the shore.

sentences.latin: Ipse certe implicitus morbo futura praeteritis, adversa secundis auguratus, spem salutis nullo suorum desperante proiecit.
sentences.english: He himself, certainly, when he was caught up in illness, judging the future from the past, the bad from the good, threw away all hope of recovery, though none of his own people was despairing.

sentences.latin: Iam illud nonne et magis terribile et non minus mirum est quod exponam ut accepi?
sentences.english: Now is not this story I will tell as I received it both more terrifying and no less wonderful?

sentences.latin: Erat Athenis spatiosa et capax domus sed infamis et pestilens.
sentences.english: There was at Athens a spacious and roomy house, but ill-omened and unhealthy.

sentences.latin: Per silentium noctis sonus ferri, et si attenderes acrius, strepitus vinculorum longius primo, deinde e proximo reddebatur: mox apparebat idolon, senex macie et squalore confectus, promissa barba horrenti capillo; cruribus compedes, manibus catenas gerebat quatiebatque.
sentences.english: Through the silence of the night the sound of iron, and if you listened more carefully, the rattling of chains was given back, at first further off, then close at hand: soon a phantom appeared, an old man wasted with thinness and squalor, with a long beard and bristling hair; on his legs he wore fetters, on his hands chains, and he kept rattling them.

sentences.latin: Inde inhabitantibus tristes diraeque noctes per metum vigilabantur; vigiliam morbus et crescente formidine mors sequebatur.
sentences.english: Hence sad and dreadful nights were passed sleepless by the inhabitants through fear; illness followed the sleeplessness, and as the dread grew, death.

sentences.latin: Nam interdiu quoque, quamquam abscesserat imago, memoria imaginis oculis inerrabat, longiorque causis timoris timor erat.
sentences.english: For even by day, although the apparition had withdrawn, the memory of the apparition wandered before their eyes, and the fear was longer-lasting than its causes.

sentences.latin: Deserta inde et damnata solitudine domus totaque illi monstro relicta; proscribebatur tamen, seu quis emere seu quis conducere ignarus tanti mali vellet.
sentences.english: Hence the house was deserted and condemned to solitude and left entirely to that monster; nevertheless it was advertised, in case anyone unaware of such a great evil should wish to buy or to rent it.

sentences.latin: Venit Athenas philosophus Athenodorus, legit titulum auditoque pretio, quia suspecta vilitas, percunctatus omnia docetur ac nihilo minus, immo tanto magis conducit.
sentences.english: The philosopher Athenodorus came to Athens, read the placard, and when he heard the price, since the cheapness was suspicious, he inquired and was told everything, and rents it nonetheless, indeed all the more.

sentences.latin: Ubi coepit advesperascere, iubet sterni sibi in prima domus parte, poscit pugillares stilum lumen; suos omnes in interiora dimittit; ipse ad scribendum animum oculos manum intendit, ne vacua mens audita simulacra et inanes sibi metus fingeret.
sentences.english: When it began to grow dark, he orders a couch to be made for him in the front part of the house; he asks for tablets, a stylus, a lamp; he sends all his people into the inner rooms; he himself directs his mind, eyes, and hand to writing, lest his empty mind should fashion for itself the apparitions he had heard about and empty fears.

sentences.latin: Initio, quale ubique, silentium noctis; dein concuti ferrum, vincula moveri.
sentences.english: At first, the silence of the night, such as everywhere; then iron rattles, chains are moved.

sentences.latin: Ille non tollere oculos, non remittere stilum, sed offirmare animum auribusque praetendere.
sentences.english: He does not lift his eyes, does not put down his stylus, but steels his mind and stops up his ears.

sentences.latin: Tum crebrescere fragor, adventare et iam ut in limine, iam ut intra limen audiri.
sentences.english: Then the noise grew louder, came nearer, and was now heard as if at the threshold, now as if within the threshold.

sentences.latin: Respicit, videt agnoscitque narratam sibi effigiem.
sentences.english: He looks back, sees, and recognizes the figure that had been described to him.

sentences.latin: Stabat innuebatque digito similis vocanti.
sentences.english: It was standing and was beckoning with its finger like one calling.

sentences.latin: Hic contra ut paulum exspectaret manu significat rursusque ceris et stilo incumbit; illa scribentis capiti catenis insonabat.
sentences.english: He, on the contrary, signals with his hand that it should wait a moment, and again leans over his wax tablets and stylus; the figure was rattling its chains over the head of the writer.

sentences.latin: Respicit rursus idem quod prius innuentem, nec moratus tollit lumen et sequitur.
sentences.english: He looks back again, the apparition beckoning the same way as before, and without delay he picks up the lamp and follows.

sentences.latin: Ibat illa lento gradu quasi gravis vinculis.
sentences.english: It went with a slow step as if heavy with its chains.

sentences.latin: Postquam deflexit in aream domus, repente dilapsa deserit comitem.
sentences.english: After it turned aside into the courtyard of the house, suddenly it slipped away and abandoned its companion.

sentences.latin: Desertus herbas et folia concerpta signum loco ponit.
sentences.english: Left alone, he places plucked grass and leaves as a marker on the spot.

sentences.latin: Postero die adit magistratus, monet ut illum locum effodi iubeant.
sentences.english: On the next day he goes to the magistrates and advises them to order that place to be dug up.

sentences.latin: Inveniuntur ossa inserta catenis et implicita, quae corpus aevo terraque putrefactum nuda et exesa reliquerat vinculis; collecta publice sepeliuntur.
sentences.english: Bones are found, set into chains and entwined, which the body, decayed by age and earth, had left bare and gnawed away in their fetters; gathered up, they are buried at public expense.

sentences.latin: Domus postea rite conditis manibus caruit.
sentences.english: After the spirits were duly laid to rest, the house was free.

sentences.latin: Et haec quidem affirmantibus credo; illud affirmare aliis possum.
sentences.english: These things indeed I believe on the testimony of those who affirm them; the following I can affirm to others.

sentences.latin: Est libertus mihi non illitteratus.
sentences.english: I have a freedman who is not unlettered.

sentences.latin: Cum hoc minor frater eodem lecto quiescebat.
sentences.english: His younger brother used to sleep in the same bed with him.

sentences.latin: Is visus est sibi cernere quendam in toro residentem, admoventemque capiti suo cultros, atque etiam ex ipso vertice amputantem capillos.
sentences.english: He seemed to himself to see someone sitting on the bed and bringing scissors to his head, and even cutting off hair from the very crown.

sentences.latin: Ubi illuxit, ipse circa verticem tonsus, capilli iacentes reperiuntur.
sentences.english: When day broke, he himself was found shorn around the crown, and the cut hair was found lying there.

sentences.latin: Exiguum temporis medium, et rursus simile aliud priori fidem fecit.
sentences.english: A short interval of time, and again something similar gave credibility to the first event.

sentences.latin: Puer in paedagogio mixtus pluribus dormiebat.
sentences.english: A boy was sleeping in the slave-quarters mixed in with many others.

sentences.latin: Venerunt per fenestras (ita narrat) in tunicis albis duo, cubantemque detonderunt et qua venerant recesserunt.
sentences.english: Two figures came in through the windows (so he relates) in white tunics, and they sheared the boy as he lay and went back the way they had come.

sentences.latin: Hunc quoque tonsum sparsosque circa capillos dies ostendit.
sentences.english: Day showed this boy too shorn and the hair scattered around him.

sentences.latin: Nihil notabile secutum, nisi forte quod non fui reus, futurus, si Domitianus sub quo haec acciderunt diutius vixisset.
sentences.english: Nothing notable followed, except perhaps that I was not put on trial, though I would have been, if Domitian, under whom these things happened, had lived longer.

sentences.latin: Nam in scrinio eius datus a Caro de me libellus inventus est; ex quo coniectari potest, quia reis moris est summittere capillum, recisos meorum capillos depulsi quod imminebat periculi signum fuisse.
sentences.english: For in his writing-case was found a charge brought against me by Carus; from which it can be conjectured that, since it is the custom for defendants to let their hair grow, the cutting of my people's hair was a sign of the danger which was threatening having been averted.

sentences.latin: Proinde rogo, eruditionem tuam intendas.
sentences.english: Therefore I ask you to apply your learning.

sentences.latin: Digna res est quam diu multumque consideres; ne ego quidem indignus, cui copiam scientiae tuae facias.
sentences.english: The matter is worthy of long and serious consideration; nor am I myself unworthy that you should share with me the abundance of your knowledge.

sentences.latin: Licet etiam utramque in partem (ut soles) disputes, ex altera tamen fortius, ne me suspensum incertumque dimittas, cum mihi consulendi causa fuerit, ut dubitare desinerem.
sentences.english: You may even argue both sides of the case (as you usually do), but argue the more strongly on one side, lest you send me away in suspense and uncertainty, since the reason for consulting you was that I might cease to doubt.

sentences.latin: Vale.
sentences.english: Farewell.
